commentary:
Risk tone ends a turbulent week on the front foot in the US and Asia, and the reason is sitting in the energy complex: crude is retreating hard, with Brent off 2.4% to $102.3 and WTI back near $100, dragging heating oil, gasoil and RBOB down with it. The Iran risk premium is bleeding out — Brent put volumes hit a six-week high, implied vol eased and call skews are the least bullish in over a week — though reports warn the "Trump backs down" playbook has been failing this month, so the tape stays headline-sensitive. Softer oil eases the inflation math just days after the Fed hiked, and that's why Nasdaq futures lead Wall Street gains (+0.5%) even as Europe trades heavy.

The other overnight story is the BoJ, which raised its call rate to 1.25% — the highest since 1995 — on a 7-2 vote, yet the yen fell over 1% to a two-week low as Ueda sent mixed signals on further hikes. That underwhelming hawkishness sits inside a broader global tightening regime: UBS flipped its BoE call to hikes reaching 4.25%, and European rate paper reflects it — Bunds, OATs and gilts all lower, front-end euro contracts soft — while the US long bond catches a modest bid despite fiscal-crisis warnings around Treasuries' historic drawdown.

Transmission-wise, precious metals remain the standout hedge in this higher-rates, sticky-inflation world: silver +2.5%, palladium +2.8%, gold firm above $4,400. TTF bucked the energy selloff (+1.4%) with EU storage at 69% versus 80%-plus last year. The soy complex and cattle sold off broadly; cocoa dropped 3.5%. Watch Iran headlines, oil vol, and BoJ follow-through on the yen.
